name: Austrian Habsburg court
summary: The dynastic center around Ferdinand II, concerned with hereditary lands, imperial title, Catholic restoration, and family security.

name: Spanish Habsburg monarchy
summary: Catholic Habsburg partner whose strategic concerns included the Dutch war and the route between Italy, the Rhine, and the Low Countries.

name: Catholic League
summary: A Catholic princely alliance led by Bavaria that supplied military capacity while creating dependence and leverage.

name: Bavaria
summary: A powerful Catholic principality led by Maximilian, useful to Ferdinand but not simply subordinate to him.

name: Bohemian estates
summary: Noble and estate interests defending privileges, religious concessions, and political participation in Bohemia.

name: Electoral Palatinate
summary: Calvinist electoral principality whose leader Frederick V accepted the Bohemian crown and became the focus of imperial punishment.

name: Saxony
summary: A leading Lutheran electorate balancing legal order, Protestant caution, imperial cooperation, and territorial security.

name: Imperial Diet and imperial constitution
summary: The legal-political order that limited imperial action and made legitimacy matter even when military victory was available.

name: Mercenary officer corps
summary: Military entrepreneurs and officers whose armies solved immediate force problems while creating fiscal and social devastation.
